_comment: The Analysis page of the QuEst window (analysis_card.py), drawn by emtk. Top-level panels are dock windows: the run settings on the left, the results on the right. Tables read the declared columns of settings/analysis/*.yaml through columns_source; custom 'analysis_plot' sections are the card's implot drawings, named by target.

sections.title: Analysis
sections.description: Which measurements are analysed, how thoroughly, and the run.
Load the shipped MalE measurements, or pick a folder of your own.

buttons.label: Load example
buttons.description: Load the shipped MalE data set (nine labelled sites, three dyes, apo and holo, H2O and D2O, plus the free-dye amino-acid titrations) and choose the quick preset.

buttons.label: Data folder…
buttons.description: Pick a folder holding the three measurement tables: tcspc_fit_results.csv, amino_acid_quenching_flt.csv and titration_summary.csv (the layout of examples/male).

sections.label: Data
sections.placeholder: press Load example, or pick a data folder
sections.description: The measurement folder being analysed. Its three CSV tables are read when the folder is chosen; the titrations, lifetimes and kQ per dye are shown at once, before any fit.

sections.label: Preset
descriptions: 8 searches with short iterations and a 7-point profile: about 20 minutes on a desktop, for a first look; the numbers are less reliable.
64 searches and the full joint fit, as the stored analysis: hours on a desktop (the stored run took 24 minutes on 44 cores).
sections.description: How thoroughly the inverse fit searches. Changing it discards the solved graphs.

sections.label: Stages
sections.description: Which stages to run: all of them in the declared order, or one stage and whatever it needs (stage A solves the joint graph, so C after A costs nothing more).

sections.label: Workers
sections.description: Worker processes for the searches and Jacobians; 0 uses every CPU, 1 runs in this process. The numbers do not depend on it.

sections.label: Profile likelihood
sections.description: Also compute the profile likelihood of the quench scale (the data set's sub-graph refitted at fixed scale values). It costs about one joint fit per point.
Run the analysis, stop it, or write its tables.

buttons.label: Run
buttons.description: Build the missing site tables and run the chosen stages in the background. The window stays usable; the bar shows how far it is.

buttons.label: Cancel
buttons.description: Stop the run at its next checkpoint (between site tables, between searches, at a joint-fit step). A search already running in a worker finishes first.

buttons.label: Write results…
buttons.description: Write every table of the stages run so far as CSV, the numbers as summary.json and the texts as report.md into a folder.

sections.description: How far the run is.
What the last action did, or why it did not.

sections.title: Results
sections.description: The measurements, their statistics and the fit results, one subject per tab.
One subject per tab.

sections.title: Data
sections.description: The titrations and the lifetimes on the protein, with the statistics derived from them.

sections.label: Dye
sections.description: The dye whose titrations and water quenching are plotted.
Stern-Volmer plot: tau0/tau - 1 of the free dye against the amino-acid concentration, every titration point, with the posterior slope K_SV of each amino acid as a line.
Posterior of the day-to-day error that all titrations share: absolute part (1/M) against relative part, on log axes. The K_SV errors are averaged over it.
The K_SV posterior of every titration and the bimolecular quenching constant kq = K_SV / tau0.
The lifetime of every labelled site, read from its heavy-water line at 0 % and 100 % D2O, with its measurement error.
Free-dye lifetimes tau0 in normal and heavy water: where every prediction starts.
Water quenching rate kq_w of the chosen dye per site (slope of 1/tau against the H2O fraction); apo and holo side by side.

sections.title: kQ per dye
sections.description: Contact quenching rate of every quenching residue for each dye, scaled from the reference chemistry by the titrations.
kQ at contact per residue (bars) and dye (colours), with its uncertainty propagated from the K_SV posterior.
kQ at contact per dye and quenching residue.

sections.title: Site tables
sections.description: The per-position features of every labelled site: accessible volume, residue neighbours, quencher contacts and water exposure.
Build the site tables without fitting.

buttons.label: Build site tables
buttons.description: Compute (or read from the cache) the site table of every measured site at each dye's linker length, in the background. A run does this first anyway.

sections.description: One row per site table the analysis holds. Select a row to see its exposure histogram.

columns.title: Dye
columns.description: Dye whose linker length the table was built at.

columns.title: Linker
columns.description: Stretched linker length of the dye.

columns.title: Positions
columns.description: Reachable dye positions (voxels of the accessible volume).

columns.title: Distinct
columns.description: Positions with distinct features; the fit evaluates these only.

columns.title: Exposure
columns.description: Mean water exposure over the reachable positions (1 = as exposed as the free dye).

columns.title: Neighbours
columns.description: Mean number of residues within the slowing radius of a position.

sections.description: Water exposure of the selected site's reachable positions (histogram over positions, not weighted by where the dye spends its time).

sections.title: Fit
sections.description: Estimates, predictions and checks of one data set of one stage.

sections.label: Stage
sections.description: The stage whose result is shown (A: AF488 and Cy3B in H2O; B: Atto655 in D2O; the naive H2O transfer test; C: Atto655 in D2O and H2O).

sections.label: Data set
sections.description: The data set of the stage (one dye in its solvents).
The stage's result in words, written from its numbers.
Predicted against measured lifetime per site: x error = measurement and model error, y error = prediction uncertainty; ringed points are outliers; dashed lines are the free-dye tau0 per solvent.
The multiplicative parameters (stickiness per group, quench scale, static channel) with their 68 % intervals, on a log axis.
Leave one site out: the largest |z| of each site's prediction when the site is left out of the fit; above the dashed line (3) a site is an outlier.
Quench scale: the profile likelihood (deviance, the sub-graph refitted at each fixed scale) and the Laplace 68 % interval.
Estimates of the data set with their 68 % intervals; a note says when a parameter is not determined or sits at a bound.
Measured and predicted lifetime of every site of the data set.
Titration slopes K_SV as measured (titrations alone) and after the graph fit (the protein lifetimes also inform them), with 68 % intervals.
The titration slopes the graph reads, measured and after the fit.

sections.title: Water
sections.description: Stage C: does the model's water exposure explain the measured difference between normal and heavy water?
Water access per site, model against measured (1 = as exposed as the free dye), with both errors.
Measured and model water access per site.
Time-weighted water exposure of the declared sites: how much of the visible dye's time is spent at each exposure.
Water exposure per site over reachable positions and over the visible dye's time.
Quench scale of Atto655 from heavy water alone (B) and from heavy and normal water together (C): profile likelihoods and Laplace intervals. Narrower in C means normal water added information.

sections.title: Summary
sections.description: What each dye tells, across the stages.
One line per dye, written from the numbers.
Quench scale of each dye's final data set with its 68 % interval, on a log axis.
Stickiness per residue group and dye (1 = not sticky, smaller = the dye lingers longer near that group), with 68 % intervals, on a log axis.
One row per dye: the quench scale, the stickiest group and the outlier sites.
